topicName: Gaseous Exchange and Respiration in Mammals
description: How mammals exchange gases in the lungs and how cells release energy from food through aerobic and anaerobic respiration, including the breathing mechanism, respiratory structures and common respiratory diseases.

mcq.questionText: Gaseous exchange in mammals takes place mainly in the:
mcq.explanation: The lungs take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide. Exam Tip: Lungs = gaseous exchange organ. Do not confuse with respiration inside cells.

mcq.questionText: The tiny air sacs in the lungs where gaseous exchange occurs are called:
mcq.explanation: These are the alveoli (singular alveolus). Exam Tip: Alveoli have thin moist walls and a rich blood supply.
The diaphragm contracts and flattens (moves down), enlarging the chest so air rushes in. Exam Tip: Inhalation: diaphragm contracts, ribs up and out, chest volume increases.

mcq.questionText: The gas taken IN by the body during breathing is:
mcq.explanation: Oxygen is taken in for respiration. Exam Tip: In: oxygen. Out: carbon dioxide.

mcq.questionText: The gas breathed OUT in greater amounts than it is breathed in is:
mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide is produced and breathed out. Exam Tip: Exhaled air has MORE CO2, less oxygen. Nitrogen stays about the same.

mcq.questionText: The chemical process by which cells release energy from food is called:
mcq.explanation: Releasing energy from food is respiration. Exam Tip: Respiration happens in cells (mitochondria). Breathing just supplies oxygen.

mcq.questionText: Respiration that takes place in the presence of oxygen is called:
mcq.explanation: Respiration using oxygen is aerobic. Exam Tip: Aerobic releases MUCH energy; products CO2 and water. Anaerobic releases little.

mcq.questionText: The word equation for aerobic respiration is: glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + __________.
mcq.explanation: The purpose is to release energy. Exam Tip: glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy (reverse of photosynthesis).

mcq.questionText: Anaerobic respiration in human muscles during hard exercise produces:
mcq.explanation: Without enough oxygen, glucose is partly broken down to lactic acid. Exam Tip: Human muscle anaerobic -> lactic acid; yeast -> alcohol + CO2.

mcq.questionText: Anaerobic respiration in yeast (used in baking and brewing) produces alcohol and:
mcq.explanation: Yeast fermentation produces ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide. Exam Tip: The CO2 makes bread rise; the alcohol is used in brewing.

mcq.questionText: Which feature of the alveoli makes them efficient for gaseous exchange?

options.text: Thin, moist walls with a rich blood supply

mcq.explanation: Alveoli have thin moist walls and many capillaries. Exam Tip: Alveoli adaptations: large surface area, thin moist walls, rich blood supply.

mcq.questionText: During exhalation (breathing out), the volume of the chest cavity:
mcq.explanation: The diaphragm relaxes and rises, ribs down and in, so chest volume decreases. Exam Tip: Exhalation: chest volume decreases -> air pushed out.

mcq.questionText: Compared with aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration releases:
mcq.explanation: Anaerobic does not fully break down glucose, so releases much LESS energy. Exam Tip: Aerobic = lots of energy; anaerobic = little energy.

mcq.questionText: The tube that carries air from the throat towards the lungs, kept open by rings of cartilage, is the:
mcq.explanation: This is the trachea (windpipe), held open by cartilage rings. Exam Tip: Trachea -> bronchi -> bronchioles -> alveoli.

mcq.questionText: A disease of the respiratory system caused by bacteria and affecting the lungs is:
mcq.explanation: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that damages the lungs. Exam Tip: Respiratory: TB, pneumonia, asthma, bronchitis. Malaria/anaemia/scurvy are not respiratory.

fib.questionText: Gaseous exchange in mammals takes place in the air sacs called __________.
fib.explanation: The alveoli are the air sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged. Exam Tip: Alveoli provide a huge thin moist surface.

fib.questionText: The gas taken into the body for respiration is __________.
fib.explanation: Oxygen is taken in and used by cells to release energy. Exam Tip: Oxygen in; carbon dioxide out.

fib.questionText: The chemical process by which cells release energy from glucose is called __________.
fib.explanation: Respiration is the release of energy from glucose inside cells. Exam Tip: Respiration occurs in the mitochondria of cells.

fib.questionText: Respiration that occurs in the presence of oxygen is called __________ respiration.
fib.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to fully break down glucose. Exam Tip: Aerobic releases much energy; products CO2 and water.

fib.questionText: During hard exercise, anaerobic respiration in human muscles produces __________ acid.
fib.explanation: With too little oxygen, muscles break glucose down only as far as lactic acid. Exam Tip: Lactic acid build-up causes muscle fatigue.

fib.questionText: The muscular sheet below the lungs that helps in breathing is the __________.
fib.explanation: The diaphragm changes the chest volume to move air in and out. Exam Tip: Contracts (flattens) for inhalation; relaxes (domes up) for exhalation.

fib.questionText: The gas produced as a waste product of respiration and breathed out is __________.
fib.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the waste gas from respiration and is removed in exhaled air. Exam Tip: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.

fib.questionText: In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) produces carbon dioxide and __________.
fib.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide when oxygen is absent. Exam Tip: Yeast -> alcohol + CO2; the CO2 makes bread rise.

fib.questionText: The windpipe, held open by rings of cartilage, is also called the __________.
fib.explanation: The trachea carries air to the lungs and is kept open by cartilage rings. Exam Tip: Cartilage rings keep the trachea from collapsing.

fib.questionText: Aerobic respiration releases __________ energy than anaerobic respiration from the same glucose.
fib.explanation: Aerobic respiration breaks glucose down completely, so it releases more energy. Exam Tip: Aerobic = more energy; anaerobic = less energy.

tf.questionText: Gaseous exchange in mammals takes place in the alveoli of the lungs.
tf.explanation: Alveoli are the sites of gaseous exchange in the lungs. Exam Tip: Alveoli have thin moist walls and a rich blood supply.

tf.questionText: During inhalation, the diaphragm relaxes and moves upward.
tf.explanation: During inhalation the diaphragm contracts and flattens (moves down); relaxing and moving up happens during exhalation. Exam Tip: Inhalation = diaphragm contracts/flattens (down). This describes exhalation.

tf.questionText: Respiration is the process by which cells release energy from food.
tf.explanation: Respiration releases energy from food inside cells. Exam Tip: Respiration (in cells) differs from breathing (moving air).

tf.questionText: Aerobic respiration takes place without oxygen.
tf.explanation: Aerobic respiration needs oxygen; respiration without oxygen is anaerobic. Exam Tip: Aerobic = WITH oxygen; anaerobic = without.

tf.questionText: Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air.
tf.explanation: Respiration produces carbon dioxide, so exhaled air is richer in it. Exam Tip: Exhaled air: more CO2, less oxygen, more water vapour.

tf.questionText: Anaerobic respiration in human muscles produces alcohol.
tf.explanation: Human muscles produce lactic acid, not alcohol; alcohol is produced by yeast. Exam Tip: Human muscle -> lactic acid; yeast -> alcohol.

tf.questionText: Breathing and respiration mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: Breathing is the mechanical movement of air, while respiration is the chemical release of energy in cells. Exam Tip: Breathing (mechanical) is not respiration (chemical).

tf.questionText: Aerobic respiration releases more energy than anaerobic respiration.
tf.explanation: Complete breakdown of glucose in aerobic respiration releases more energy. Exam Tip: More complete breakdown -> more energy.

tf.questionText: The alveoli have thin, moist walls to allow easy diffusion of gases.
tf.explanation: Thin, moist walls shorten the diffusion path so gases move quickly. Exam Tip: Alveoli adaptations aid diffusion.

tf.questionText: Tuberculosis (TB) is a disease of the respiratory system.
tf.explanation: TB is a bacterial disease that attacks the lungs. Exam Tip: Respiratory: TB, pneumonia, asthma, bronchitis.

summary.correctAnswer: The lungs are the mammalian gaseous exchange organs, containing millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged.
summary.explanation: Alveoli have a large surface area, thin moist walls and a rich blood supply. Exam Tip: Lungs = organ; alveoli = actual site of gas exchange.

summary.correctAnswer: Breathing is the mechanical movement of air in and out of the lungs, driven by the diaphragm and rib muscles changing the volume of the chest cavity.
summary.explanation: The diaphragm is a muscular sheet below the lungs that flattens or domes to change chest volume. Exam Tip: Bigger chest volume draws air in; smaller volume pushes it out.

summary.correctAnswer: In inhalation the diaphragm contracts and moves down, ribs move up and out, and chest volume increases so air rushes in; in exhalation the diaphragm relaxes and moves up, ribs move down and in, and chest volume decreases so air is pushed out.
summary.explanation: Air always moves from high to low pressure created by these volume changes. Exam Tip: Inhalation increases volume; exhalation decreases volume.

summary.correctAnswer: Respiration is the chemical process in which cells release energy from food such as glucose.
summary.explanation: It takes place in the mitochondria of cells and is different from breathing. Exam Tip: Do not confuse respiration (chemical) with breathing (mechanical).

summary.correctAnswer: Aerobic respiration is the release of energy from glucose using oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and water and a large amount of energy.
summary.explanation: It fully breaks down glucose, so it yields much more energy than anaerobic respiration. Exam Tip: Aerobic = with oxygen = lots of energy.

summary.correctAnswer: glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy
summary.explanation: This word equation is the reverse of photosynthesis. Exam Tip: Learn this equation exactly; energy is always the key product.

summary.questionText: Anaerobic respiration in muscle and lactic acid
summary.correctAnswer: Anaerobic respiration in human muscles occurs when oxygen is short, partly breaking down glucose into lactic acid and releasing a small amount of energy.
summary.explanation: Lactic acid build-up causes muscle fatigue and an oxygen debt repaid by heavy breathing afterwards. Exam Tip: Muscle anaerobic -> lactic acid + little energy.

summary.questionText: Anaerobic respiration in yeast and fermentation
summary.correctAnswer: Anaerobic respiration in yeast, called fermentation, breaks down sugar into alcohol (ethanol) and carbon dioxide with little energy released.
summary.explanation: The carbon dioxide makes bread rise and the alcohol is used in brewing. Exam Tip: Yeast anaerobic -> alcohol + CO2.

summary.correctAnswer: The trachea, or windpipe, is the tube that carries air from the throat towards the lungs and is kept open by rings of cartilage.
summary.explanation: Air passes from the trachea into the bronchi, then bronchioles, then alveoli. Exam Tip: Cartilage rings stop the trachea collapsing.

summary.correctAnswer: Respiratory diseases are illnesses affecting the breathing system, such as tuberculosis (TB), pneumonia, asthma and bronchitis.
summary.explanation: TB is caused by bacteria and damages the lungs. Exam Tip: Malaria, anaemia and scurvy are NOT respiratory diseases.

hoq.questionText: A student breathes out through a straw into limewater and it turns milky, but freshly inhaled air passed through separate limewater stays clear much longer. What does this show?

options.text: Inhaled air has more carbon dioxide
Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air, because respiration produces carbon dioxide

hoq.explanation: Limewater turns milky with CO2. Exhaled air turns it milky quickly, showing it is rich in CO2 from respiration. Exam Tip: Limewater is the test for carbon dioxide (milky = CO2 present).

hoq.questionText: A footballer sprints hard. Her muscles ache and she keeps breathing heavily for minutes AFTER stopping. Explain using aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

options.text: During the sprint, oxygen ran short, so muscles used anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid (causing ache); afterwards she breathes heavily to take in extra oxygen to break down the lactic acid
Lactic acid gives her energy directly

hoq.explanation: Oxygen shortage forces anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid (ache). Heavy breathing afterwards repays the oxygen debt to remove the lactic acid. Exam Tip: Hard exercise -> oxygen shortage -> anaerobic -> lactic acid -> fatigue. Panting afterwards removes it with oxygen.

hoq.questionText: Yeast is mixed with sugar solution, a little oil is added on top to keep out air, and the gas produced is passed through limewater. The limewater turns milky, and after a day the mixture smells of alcohol. Explain.

options.text: The yeast carried out aerobic respiration
With air kept out, the yeast carried out anaerobic respiration (fermentation), producing carbon dioxide (turns limewater milky) and alcohol (the smell)

hoq.explanation: The oil keeps oxygen out, so conditions are anaerobic. Yeast ferments sugar into carbon dioxide (milky limewater) and alcohol (smell). Exam Tip: The OIL layer excludes oxygen, forcing anaerobic respiration. Yeast -> alcohol + CO2.
